serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Replit for Government is a cloud platform that lets
government organizations securely build, run and deploy
software with the help of AI. It combines , an AI agent that
plans, builds, tests and changes applications from natural-
language prompts, with a Cloud Development Environment
that gives each user an isolated cloud workspace with a
persistent filesystem, in-browser and SSH access, real-time
collaboration and AI coding assistance. Through Replit
Deployments,
Users can deploy applications that are immediately
shareable with your teams on a secure platform for mission
critical federal systems..

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: FedRAMP Trust Center for the Cloud Service Offering.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
Agencies can request access by emailing **security@repl.it
or security@replit.com**. Replit's GRC team reviews each
request and grants access to the FedRAMP certification
data in the trust center.
trustCenter.agencyAccessDenialProcess:
Agencies send access requests to security@repl.it. GRC
logs and reviews each request. If GRC denies a request,
GRC notifies FedRAMP within 5 business days through the
"[CSP] Agency Access Denial" form, including the agency
name, request date, denial date and reason. GRC also
notifies the requesting agency and keeps a record of each
request, decision and notification.

informationResources.summary:
The offering matches the system boundary of Replit's SOC 2
Type II examination of its Cloud Services and Cloud
Development Environment. It runs on Google Cloud
Platform and includes the infrastructure, software, data,
people and procedures that directly support Replit Agent,
the Cloud Development Environment and Replit
Deployments. Resources listed below are those likely to
handle federal customer data or to affect its confidentiality,
integrity or availability. Third-party services are described in
Section 8.
informationResources.explicitExclusions:
Replit mobile and desktop apps, which are software installed
on user devices and outside the scope of FedRAMP A. We
will plan to include this in scope as we move forward.
Internal corporate systems that do not support delivery of
the service, such as HR, payroll and recruiting tools.

resources.name: Google Cloud production infrastructure
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Google Kubernetes Engine, Compute Engine, Cloud
Storage, Cloud SQL and related Google Cloud services that
host all Replit services and store customer data.

resources.name: Replit web application and API
resources.descriptionAndRole:
The replit.com web application and GraphQL API that users
and administrators use to access the service.

resources.name: Cloud Development Environment runtime
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Isolated per-user microVMs and the control plane that create
and run cloud workspaces and store project files.

resources.name: Replit Agent and AI model proxy
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Services that run Replit Agent and route prompts and
workspace content to AI model providers.

resources.name: Replit Deployments hosting
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Infrastructure that builds and runs customer applications as
Reserved VM, Autoscale and Static deployments.

resources.name: User authentication services
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Firebase (Google Identity Platform) for user sign-in and
WorkOS for customer single sign-on.

resources.name: Key and secrets management
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Google Cloud KMS, Google Secret Manager and HashiCorp
Vault, which hold encryption keys and service secrets.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Protects the confidentiality and integrity of customer data by
controlling the keys and secrets used to encrypt and access
it.

resources.name: Logging and monitoring
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Datadog, Sentry and Google Cloud logging, which collect
system logs, metrics, traces and error reports. Logs may
include customer data.

resources.name: Source control and CI/CD
resources.descriptionAndRole:
GitHub, Semaphore, Harness and Argo CD, which store
source code and deploy changes to production.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Affects integrity and availability because these systems build
and deploy the code that runs the service.

resources.name: Workforce identity and device management
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Okta for workforce single sign-on and MFA, plus endpoint
management for employee devices.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Affects confidentiality and integrity because it controls which
Replit personnel can access production systems.

resources.name: Replit operations and support personnel
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Security, SRE, engineering and support staff who operate
the service and respond to incidents and customer requests.

alternativeSecurityFramework.impactLevelScope:
SOC 2 Type II, Security Trust Services Criteria. System:
Replit Cloud Services and Cloud Development Environment.
Examination period: June 2, 2024 to October 31, 2025.
alternativeSecurityFramework.mappingToFedRampRules:
FRC-CSO-PKG and FRC-CSO-JSN: Replit is preparing this
package and the required JSON files with Paramify.
FRC-CSO-POP: Replit has selected the FedRAMP 20x path
and is not pursuing Rev5 for this offering.
MAS-CSO-IIR: Scope matches the SOC 2 system boundary.
See Section 6.
CDS-CSO-PUB and CDS-CSO-UTC: Public information and
certification data will be published through a FedRAMP-
compatible trust center on Paramify.
CDS-UTC-AAD: GRC owns a documented procedure to
notify FedRAMP within 5 business days of denying an
agency access request. See Section 2.
AFC-CSO-INB, AFC-CSO-RCV and AFC-CSO-CRA:
security@repl.it is the FedRAMP Security Inbox. It is a
shared inbox reviewed by the Security team, who will act on
FedRAMP Emergency and Emergency Test messages
within the stated timeframes.
IEC-CSO-EFR and IEC-CSO-FIR: Replit follows its Incident
Response Plan (v1.3, effective September 11, 2026), using
Rootly to log, track and communicate incidents. The SOC 2
auditor tested incident logging, tracking and communication
with no exceptions. Replit will add a step to evaluate
whether incidents affect federal customer data and will issue
Final Incident Reports within 3 business days of resolution.
VDR-CSO-DET: Replit scans source code and
dependencies, uses Wiz for cloud security and vulnerability
scanning, scans external-facing systems at least quarterly,
runs an annual third-party penetration test and operates a
private bug bounty program. Datadog and Cloudflare
provide intrusion detection. The SOC 2 auditor noted
exceptions in tracking critical and high findings to
remediation and in patch timing.
CCM-OCR-AVL and CCM-OCR-NRD: Replit will produce an
Ongoing Certification Report every 3 months and publish the
next report date.
IVV-CSX-AIA: Replit maintains an annual SOC 2 Type II
examination with Prescient Assurance. The current
examination period runs from November 1, 2025 to October
31, 2026.
KSI-CMT-LMC: Changes go through tickets, testing,
approval and version control, and CI/CD deployments are
logged and monitored with alerts. Tested by the SOC 2
auditor with no exceptions (CC7.2, CC8.1).
KSI-CNA-RNT: Production containers are firewalled and
external traffic enters only through designated HTTPS
frontends. Firewall rules are reviewed at least annually.
Tested with no exceptions (CC6.6).
KSI-CED-RAT: All employees complete security awareness
training in KnowBe4 within 30 days of hire and annually.
Tested with no exceptions (CC1.4, CC2.2).
KSI-IAM-AAM: Okta is the workforce identity provider, with
automated provisioning through SCIM for connected
applications. Access is removed within 24 hours of
termination and reviewed periodically. Tested with no
exceptions (CC6.2, CC6.3).
KSI-IAM-APM: Okta enforces single sign-on and MFA for in-
scope systems. Okta FastPass passwordless sign-in is
available. Tested with no exceptions (CC6.1, CC6.6).
KSI-INR-RIR: The Incident Response Plan requires at least
annual testing with lessons learned recorded. Annual
tabletop exercises were tested with no exceptions (CC7.4,
CC7.5).
KSI-SVC-SIN: Data is encrypted in transit with TLS and at
rest through Google Cloud encryption and Cloud KMS.
Backups are encrypted, access is role-based with SSO and
MFA, and customer data is deleted under a retention policy.
Tested with no exceptions (CC6.1 to CC6.6).

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
AI agent that plans, builds, tests and changes applications
from natural-language prompts inside the user's cloud
workspace.

Isolated cloud workspaces with a persistent filesystem for
writing, running and testing code, with in-browser and SSH
access, real-time collaboration and AI coding assistance.

Hosting for applications built on Replit, offered as Reserved
VM, Autoscale and Static deployments, each with a build
and deployment step.

thirdPartyInformationResources.metadataIncludedInScope:
Yes. Metadata about federal customer data, such as
account, usage, audit log and system log metadata, is
included in the scope of the offering.

certified.fedRampCertifiedThirdPartyInformationRes:
FR1805751477 (Google Services: Google Cloud Platform
Products and underlying Infrastructure)
certified.useCase:
Hosts all Replit compute, storage, databases, key
management and Vertex AI model inference.
certified.usageAndConfiguration:
Replit-managed Google Cloud projects running Google
Kubernetes Engine, Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud
SQL, Cloud KMS, Secret Manager and Vertex AI.
certified.justificationForUse:
Primary infrastructure provider for the offering, with an
existing FedRAMP certification.
certified.mitigationMeasures:
Data is encrypted at rest with Google default encryption and
Cloud KMS and in transit with TLS. Access uses least-
privilege IAM roles and is logged.
certified.compensatingControls:
Replit reviews Google's attestation reports at least annually
and performs a risk analysis of Google Cloud Platform.
